title: Section algebra tensors and canonical intersection comparison
statement: For a scheme $Y$ [def-pc-scheme] and opens $(U_i)_{i\in I}$, write $E=\bigcap_i U_i$ and $C=\Gamma(E,\mathcal O_Y|_E)$ [def-a1-intersection-structure-sections]. A scheme map $g:X\to Y$ carrying $F=\bigcap_j V_j$ into $E$ induces the continuous map $F\to E$ and the map of inverse-image structure sheaves [def-weil-pbc-topological-inverse-image] obtained by adjunction from its scheme comorphism; evaluation on the whole subspace gives $g_E^\sharp:C\to\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_X|_F)$. For $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], define the scalar map $R\to C$ by global sections of $f$ followed by restriction, and give $C$ this $R$-algebra structure. For a ring map $r:R\to T$ and any $R$-algebra $B$, define its scalar extension $B\otimes_R T$, with the $T$-algebra structure from the right factor and pure tensors $b\otimes t$; in particular the tensor source for $f,E$ is $C\otimes_R T$. For $q:X\to\operatorname{Spec}T$ satisfying $f\circ g=\operatorname{Spec}(r)\circ q$, define the canonical $T$-algebra homomorphism $C\otimes_R T\to\Gamma(F,\mathcal O_X|_F)$ by $c\otimes t\mapsto g_E^\sharp(c)q_F^\sharp(t)$. Its specialization to $X=Y\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $g$ and $q$ the projections and $V_i=g^{-1}U_i$, is the canonical intersection base-change map. No flatness, compactness, or nonemptiness condition is part of these definitions.
